finding: Resume calls start_generation without re-checking the user's provider-group access to model_id. create_provider_from_model_id only checks provider.enabled, not user_has_access_to_provider; the scheduler re-checks it at fire time (dispatch.rs:319-335) as a blind-audit fix. A user removed from the provider group between spawn and completion still gets the model driven by the resumed turn. The spawn_subagent comment claiming create_provider_from_model_id re-checks RBAC is inaccurate.

Sub-agent final_text (model-produced, possibly derived from untrusted web/bio/lit tool output) is injected as a USER-role message with authoritative framing, elevating tool-result-trust content to user-role in the parent conversation (prompt-injection surface). Chosen approach (DEC-1) but the trust elevation is real; add an untrusted-content guard line.

The resumed turn (enable_mcp:true, not unattended) can itself spawn ANOTHER background subagent whose completion resumes again — a chain with no explicit depth cap. TEST-6 proves a single completion fires once, not that the chain is bounded.

resume_conversation_with_result takes three adjacent same-typed positional Uuid params (user_id, conversation_id, model_id) — a transposition footgun the type system can't catch (flagged by two independent angles).

TEST-5 proves a resumed assistant reply only via any(role==assistant) — existence, not content. A started-but-empty assistant row satisfies it; narrower than the TESTS.md prose 'a fresh assistant reply'. Assert the assistant reply carries the stub answer.

RESUME_MAX_IDLE_WAIT docstring claims it 'mirrors the scheduler's fixed-const headless-turn wait (TERMINAL_WAIT)', but both the value (5min vs 15min) and the semantics (wait-for-idle-before-start vs wait-for-terminal-after-start) differ; the mirror claim is misleading.

On idle-wait timeout resume returns Err (skip), whereas the scheduler wait loop it cites break's best-effort and proceeds. Divergence is defensible (idle-before-start), but the 'mirrors scheduler/dispatch.rs wait loop' comment overstates the parallel.

The truncation pointer text says 'call collect_result with this run's run_id for the full output', but run_id is never a parameter of build_resume_message / resume_conversation_with_result and is not embedded, so the injected turn cannot surface the concrete run_id.

The detached resume tokio::spawn stores no JoinHandle and has no cancellation (CODING_GUIDELINES §5); bounded by RESUME_MAX_IDLE_WAIT (5min) so not unbounded, but sleeping tasks are orphaned on shutdown rather than cancelled.

TESTS.md file attributions are stale: TEST-4's should_resume test ships in resume.rs (not tools.rs), and TEST-5 reads messages via REST GET /conversations/{id}/messages (not get_message_with_content as the prose says). Coverage is present; the attributions need updating.

Truncation is char-boundary safe (chars().take/collect); tokio::spawn captures all owned; resume reaches both legacy+agent-core via start_generation's ZIEE_CHAT_AGENT_CORE dispatch; .expect(should_resume guarantees Some) is sound.
Every ?/ok_or_else propagates to the caller which only tracing::warn!s — a resume failure cannot fail the already-Completed run. Log-and-continue intact.
OnceCell set-once via let _ = set(); background_mcp_config() returns Option; resume None-errors safely.
wait-for-idle 500ms poll is deadline-bounded (5min); char cap O(n); no unbounded loop.
resume.rs is self-contained; cross-module reach matches the scheduler precedent; the tools.rs hook cleanly delegates (gate+capture+spawn only).
should_resume is kind-agnostic and the subagent gate is structural (hook placement), not a closed match — a new resuming kind adds its own hook call.
Only tool description strings changed; inputSchema/required shapes unchanged; no OpenAPI type/route change.
